overview: This bill, the Patients Deserve Price Tags Act, aims to make health care prices easier to see before patients get care. It would write into law and expand requirements that hospitals post their prices online, including cash prices and the rates they have negotiated with each insurer, and would extend similar rules to labs, imaging centers, and outpatient surgery centers, along with disclosing who owns them. Hospitals that don't comply could face daily fines, and a senior executive would have to vouch for the accuracy of the posted prices. Health plans would have to give enrollees clearer cost information, and employers with large health plans would gain more access to data about what their plans pay. Patients would be protected from paying bills substantially higher than an advance estimate from their insurer, and providers would have to tell patients they can request an itemized bill before pursuing collections. As of July 27, 2026, it had been approved by a Senate committee and placed on the Senate calendar.
for: Supporters say patients and employers cannot make smart choices or control costs when prices are hidden, and enforceable price posting with real penalties will help people compare and avoid surprise bills.
against: Critics say the extensive new reporting rules add costs and paperwork for hospitals, labs, and smaller providers, and posted price lists may still be too complex for most patients to use.
